sn22.84:2.2: “Venerable sir, Venerable Tissa—the Buddha’s cousin on his father’s side—informed several mendicants:
sn22.84:2.3: ‘Reverends, my body feels like it’s drugged. I’m disorientated, the teachings don’t spring to mind, and dullness and drowsiness fill my mind. I lead the spiritual life dissatisfied, and have doubts about the teachings.’”
sn22.84:4.7: when those choices of theirs decay and perish, will it give rise to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress?”
sn22.84:7.7: If you are rid of greed, desire, fondness, thirst, passion, and craving for consciousness, when that consciousness decays and perishes, will it give rise to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress?”
